_comment: bdsx events that have actually FIRED under bdsx's own hook (its real prototype) on the 1.26 builds, and how. A counter probe on the target does not count: it proves the address, never the prototype (docs/findings-slots.md, 'Changed signatures'). Read by tools/event-coverage.mjs. Add an entry only with the run tag and what the listener printed.

fired.command: tools/origin-probe.ts, tools/gamerules-probe.ts: console commands reach the listener, both builds
fired.playerJoin: originB / originB51 (2026-09-18): once per bot join, the player Player::respawn had handed over
fired.playerRespawn: originB / originB51: once per join and per kill
fired.playerLeft: originB (40), left51 (2026-09-19): once when the bot closes mid-session; NOT at a driven stop
fired.levelWeatherChange: gr40 / gr51 (2026-09-19): (1,t,0,t) rain, (1,t,1,t) thunder, (0,t,0,t) clear; Level.updateWeather() raises one
fired.entityHurt: sig40 / sig51 (2026-09-19): iron golem vs zombies, damage / cause / knock / ignite sane
fired.entityKnockback: sig40 / sig51: one after each hurt, power/height/cap 0.52/0.39/0.8 and 0.4/0.4/0.4
fired.playerDimensionChange: sig40 / sig51: to=1 on `execute in nether tp`, to=0 on the respawn back
fired.farmlandDecay: 2026-09-20, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with FARM_PROBE=1 (drivers farm40/farm51.ps1). BDS itself entered the hook 10 times on 1.26.40.8 and 3 times on 1.26.51.1 when entities landed on farmland the console had placed (minecart, boat, cow, iron_golem, zombie, item); every entry had the FarmBlock vftable as this and three of the positions read minecraft:dirt afterwards. The probe also calls the address directly through the hook with the 2024 prototype, and a CANCEL return leaves the block untouched. work/host-runs/farm40-20260920-143625.txt, farm51-20260920-143625.txt
fired.blockPlace: 2026-09-20, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with PLACE_PROBE=1 (drivers place40/place51.ps1). Fired by a direct call through the hook -- "placeprobe call" hands ?mayPlace@BlockSource@@ a real Block, the empty column at (29, 72, 14), facing 1, the bot and a Vec3, and bdsx's 2024 prototype comes back true with the event fired exactly once; the event's BlockSource vptr is the table's ??_7BlockSource@@6B@. "placeprobe cancel" then turns the same call into false. What is still missing is an engine-driven place: bdsx's onBlockPlace only fires for a ServerPlayer actor, so that needs a human client (Q7). work/host-runs/place40-20260920-165653.txt, place51-20260920-165653.txt | 2026-10-02: engine-driven as well -- a simulated player's simulateUseItemInSlotOnBlock places dirt through mayPlace and fires the event for it (simq740/simq751, "simp place"); cancelled, no block is placed.
fired.entityStartRiding: ride40 / ride51 (2026-09-21, work/host-runs/ride40-20260921-132937.txt): the hook is entered on both builds when the console runs /ride <rider> start_riding <vehicle>, once for a chicken into a minecart and once for the bot. 1.26 gave ?startRiding@Actor@@ a third argument, so the hook is on ?startRiding@Actor@@UEAA_NAEAV1@_N@Z (docs/findings-riding.md); the 2024 two-argument prototype had never been fired.
fired.entityStopRiding: ride40 / ride51 (2026-09-21): entered on both builds for /ride <rider> stop_riding (exit=true, destroyed=false) and for `kill` on a riding chicken (exit=true, destroyed=true) -- the second bool moves while the others stay, which is the four-bool prototype ?stopRiding@Actor@@QEAAX_N000@Z answering. docs/findings-riding.md.
fired.playerLevelUp: q2ev40 / q2ev51 (2026-09-21, work/host-runs/q2ev40-20260921-150403.txt): ?addLevels@Player@@UEAAXH@Z hooked with bdsx's 2024 prototype (this, int), which both 1.26 bodies still read -- edx into edi in the first five instructions on all three binaries. `xp 5L @a` enters it once with levels=5 and the bot as the player; the XP orbs the bot picks up after a death enter it again with levels=1.
fired.entityDie: q2ev40 / q2ev51 (2026-09-21): ?die@Mob@@UEAAXAEBVActorDamageSource@@@Z, 2024 prototype (this, ActorDamageSource const&), rdx read as a pointer in both 1.26 bodies. `kill @e[type=zombie]` enters it once per zombie with cause 13, and the bot's own death at the driven `kill @a` enters it with the player.
fired.playerPickupItem: q2ev40 / q2ev51 (2026-09-21): ?take@Player@@QEAA_NAEAVActor@@HH@Z, 2024 prototype (this, Actor&, int, int) -- both 1.26 bodies read r9d and rdx in the same first instructions 2024 does. Items dropped at the bot's feet by `loot spawn 29 68 14 loot loot_tables/entities/zombie.json` and by killed zombies enter it, player = the bot, itemActor = minecraft:item.
fired.levelSave: q2ev40 / q2ev51 (2026-09-21): ?save@Level@@UEAAXXZ, no arguments, 232 bytes and byte-identical on the two builds. `save hold` enters it once on both. NOTE: `save hold` without a following `save resume` leaves BDS unable to finish `stop` -- the first pair hung for 90 s and was killed.
fired.entityConsumeTotem: q2ev40 / q2ev51 (2026-09-21): ?consumeTotem@Actor@@UEAA_NXZ, no arguments. A zombie given a totem in its offhand (`replaceitem entity @e[type=zombie] slot.weapon.offhand 0 totem_of_undying 1`) and then killed enters it; ev.totem.getId() is 578 on both builds. The first pair armed only one zombie (`c=1`) and 1.26.40.8 killed a different one, so this needs every candidate armed.
fired.playerAttack: q2at40 / q2at51 (2026-09-22, docs/findings-audit.md "attack"): fired by a direct call through the corrected hook -- `sigprobe attack` hands "bdsx:Actor::attack" the bot's Player as `this`, a fresh AllocatedPointer(16) as the hidden ActorHurtResult* result, a freshly-armed iron golem one block away as victim, and ActorDamageCause.EntityAttack; the hook fires exactly once on both builds and the returned pointer echoes the result pointer we passed, with a well-formed, byte-identical {value@0=0, tag@4=0 (bool alt), allowKnockback@8=1} "not hurt" struct both times. The golem's health does not move (99 -> 99), and this is not a wrong address or prototype: the console-only bot's Abilities.getBool(AttackPlayers/AttackMobs) reads false false on both builds at the moment of the call (attack()'s own gate at 0x229649/0x21f0a0, AbilitiesComponent), the loading-screen-invulnerable state already on record in docs/findings-abilities.md. An engine-driven attack that actually lands still needs a human client that leaves the loading screen (Q7).
fired.sculkShriek: 2026-09-23, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with BLOCKEV2_PROBE=1 (drivers shriek40/shriek51.ps1). Fired by a direct call through the hook -- "shriekprobe cancel" then "shriekprobe call" hands ?_shriek@SculkShriekerBlockActorInternal@@ a real BlockSource, BlockPos(60,67,14) and the bot itself as Player, and the event fires exactly once with entity=the bot and CANCEL returned, leaving the native body unrun. "shriekprobe allow" then "shriekprobe call" lets the real body run -- the full 723-1322 byte routine (CompoundTag broadcast of the position, block state, GameEvent dispatch, the warden-summon attempt) completes on both builds with no crash and the session still ends Quit correctly. work/host-runs/shriek40-20260923-033209.txt, shriek51-20260923-033209.txt
fired.pistonCheck: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with PISTON_PROBE=1 (drivers pistonev40/pistonev51.ps1). Fired by the engine itself: a sticky piston facing up at (44,68,20), powered by a redstone block the console placed. With the listener returning CANCEL, 78-79 events at blockPos (44,69,20) (the walker argument), facing 0 1 0, and the stone never moved; after allow, the push went through. On unpowering, events with action 3. work/host-runs/pistonev40-20260924-001103.txt, pistonev51-20260924-001103.txt
fired.pistonMove: 2026-09-24, both builds, same sessions: fired by the engine once on extend (blockPos = the piston, action 1, affectedBlocks [44 69 20], facing 0 1 0; the stone then read back at y=70) and once on the sticky retract (action 3, [44 70 20]; the stone back at y=69).
fired.chestPair: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with CHEST_PROBE=1 (drivers chestev40/chestev51.ps1). Fired by the engine from a console setblock of two adjacent chests (onPlace -> _tryToPairWith, hooked by bdsx, both halves: lead false then true) and from the tick when a saved paired chest loads (pairWith hook, lead true). CANCEL leaves both chests single (isLargeChest false, still single 8 s later); allowed, each reports the other through getPairedChestPosition. work/host-runs/chestev40-20260924-003017.txt, chestev51-20260924-003323.txt
fired.sculkSensorActivate: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SCULK_PROBE=1 (drivers sculkev40/sculkev51.ps1). Fired by the engine: a sculk sensor set at (56,68,20) hears a summoned pig walking and blocks set beside it (entity = the pig; a leftover sensor at (33,68,20) fires for a wandering ocelot too). CANCEL keeps sculk_sensor_phase (Block+288) at 0 two and ten ticks later; allowed, it is 1 two ticks later. work/host-runs/sculkev40-20260924-004058.txt, sculkev51-20260924-004058.txt
fired.fallOnBlock: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with FALLON_PROBE=1 (drivers fallev40/fallev51.ps1). Fired by the engine through bdsx:BlockType::onFallOnBase: pigs dropped ten blocks onto stone (height 9.67), a hay bale (1.93, what hay lets through), slime (0, each bounce); honey fires nothing (its subscriber does not reach the base). work/host-runs/fallev40/51 same day.
fired.objectiveCreate: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SCORE_PROBE=1 (drivers score40/score51.ps1). `scoreboard objectives add` fires it with name and display name; CANCEL leaves Scoreboard::getObjective null, allowed it returns the objective.
fired.scoreReset: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SCORE_PROBE=1 (drivers score40/score51.ps1), through ?removeFromObjective@ScoreboardIdentityRef@@. `scoreboard players reset` fires it; CANCEL keeps the score (the console's `scoreboard players test` finds 7), allowed it is gone. Needed a fix in bdsx: the cancel path decayed idRef before reading it.
fired.scoreSet: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts modprobe (drivers mod40/mod51.ps1), through ?modifyScoreInObjective@ScoreboardIdentityRef@@ (1.26 prototype). `scoreboard players set @a probe_mod 10` fires it with 10; also fired by bdsx's own setPlayerScore.
fired.scoreAdd: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts modprobe (drivers mod40/mod51.ps1), through ?modifyScoreInObjective@ScoreboardIdentityRef@@ (1.26 prototype). `scoreboard players add … 5` fires it; with CANCEL the score stays 10 (console test), allowed via bdsx's addPlayerScore it becomes 105.
fired.scoreRemove: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts modprobe (drivers mod40/mod51.ps1), through ?modifyScoreInObjective@ScoreboardIdentityRef@@ (1.26 prototype). `scoreboard players remove … 3` fires it; the console then reports 7.
fired.entityHealthChange: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with HEALTH_PROBE=1 (drivers hc40/hc51.ps1), through bdsx:HealthAttributeDelegate::change. `damage @e[type=pig]` fires it (old/new health, the pig); a listener that sets newHealth = oldHealth keeps the pig at 10, letting it through leaves 7.
fired.entityCreated: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with CREATED_PROBE=1 (drivers ec40/ec51.ps1), through bdsx:ActorEventCoordinator::sendActorCreated. Every actor entering the world: `summon pig`/`summon zombie` give method 2 (Spawned), actors loaded with the world 1 (Loaded).
fired.splashPotionHit: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SPLASH_PROBE=1 (drivers sp40/sp51.ps1), through ?doOnHitEffect@ThrownPotionEffectSubcomponent@@ (SplashPotionEffectSubcomponent is gone in 1.26). A summoned splash potion over a pig in a pit fires it with potion 0; a listener changing it to 23 (Harming) takes the pig to 4, the same change plus CANCEL leaves the other pig at 10.
fired.campfireLight: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with CAMPFIRE_PROBE=1 (drivers cf40/cf51.ps1). A dispenser with flint and steel lights the campfire in front; CANCEL keeps it unlit (console testforblock), allowed it lights.
fired.campfireDouse: 2026-09-24, both builds: same sessions. Water placed on a lit campfire fires it (neighborChanged); CANCEL keeps it lit, allowed it goes out (console testforblock).
fired.projectileHit: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with PHIT_PROBE=1 (drivers ph40/ph51.ps1). A summoned arrow falling onto a pig fires it with the pig as victim; one falling onto stone with none.
fired.playerInventoryChange: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with INV_PROBE=1 (drivers inv40/inv51.ps1). replaceitem, give, clear <item> and clear each fire once with the right slot, old and new item.
fired.projectileShoot: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SHOOT_PROBE=1 (drivers shoot40/shoot51.ps1). A snow golem's snowballs fire it with the golem as shooter; an ownerless dispenser arrow does not.
fired.queryRegenerate: 2026-09-24, both builds, each run alone with enable-lan-visibility=true: tools/block-probe.ts with QUERY_PROBE=1 (drivers qrlan40/qrlan51.ps1). Fires with 0 then 1 players; the listener's maxPlayers shows in a real ping reply.
fired.blockDestroy: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sact40/sact51.ps1). A simulated player breaks stone in creative (the event fires at that position, testforblock finds air); with the listener returning CANCEL the stone stays (the event keeps firing each tick as the simulated player retries); in survival it breaks dirt with exactly one event -- GameMode::destroyBlock's hook covers SurvivalMode's thunk. Needed Item::canDestroyInCreative by slot (layouts.Item.canDestroyInCreativeSlot): its jsv threw inside the creative hook and crashed 40.
fired.playerUseItem: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sact40/sact51.ps1). A simulated player throws a snowball through simulateUseItemInSlot; the event fires with method 4 (throw), consume true.
fired.playerCrit: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sact40/sact51.ps1), through bdsx:Player::_crit (1.26's _crit takes one more int). A simulated player jumps and hits a pig on the way down; the event fires with the pig as victim.
fired.levelExplode: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with EXPLODE_PROBE=1 (drivers ex40/ex51.ps1), through Level::explode(Explosion&) -- TNT does not reach the nine-argument overload. A summoned TNT fires it (power 4); cancelled, the stone under it stays, allowed, it is destroyed.
fired.playerSleepInBed: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sbed40/sbed51.ps1). A simulated player uses a stick on a bed at midnight (simulateUseItemOnBlock -> useItemOn -> the bed -> Player::startSleepInBed); cancelled it stays awake, allowed it sleeps (Player::isSleeping).
fired.entityStartSwimming: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sswim40/sswim51.ps1). What the GameTest "swim" binding does -- a simulated player's own startSwimming virtual (40 slot 99, 51 slot 98, the shipped ?startSwimming@Player@@) -- fires it through bdsx's Player hook; cancelled, isSwimming stays false, allowed, it is true.
fired.itemUse: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers suse40/suse51.ps1), through GameMode::useItem -- 1.26 inlines ItemStack::use into it. A simulated player's snowball use fires it; cancelled, nothing is thrown (no playerUseItem, stack unchanged), allowed, playerUseItem follows.
fired.itemUseOnBlock: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers suon40/suon51.ps1), through bdsx:GameMode::useItemOn (1.26 added an eighth argument, a bool, placed differently on the two builds). A simulated player uses dirt on a floor block; cancelled nothing is placed, allowed the dirt is placed.
fired.attackBlock: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers satb40/satb51.ps1), through GameMode::startDestroyBlock (1.26 keeps no out-of-line Block::attack). A survival simulated player starting to break dirt fires it; cancelled the dirt stays, allowed it breaks. Fires once per start, where 2024's Block::attack also ran on each continueDestroyBlock.
fired.playerInteract: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sint40/sint51.ps1), through bdsx:Player::interact (1.26 returns the InteractionResult by sret). A simulated player with a bucket interacts with a cow; cancelled the bucket stays, allowed it becomes a milk bucket.
fired.chestOpen: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sblk40/sblk51.ps1), through bdsx:ChestBlock::use (the ChestBlock interact handler 1.26 registers). A simulated player's stick on a chest fires it; the effect of a cancel is not observable without a client's container UI.
fired.buttonPress: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sblk40/sblk51.ps1), through bdsx:ButtonBlock::use. A simulated player's stick on a stone button fires it; on 51 a cancel leaves the button up and an allow presses it; on 40 too, read by Block* permutation (sbtn40/51): testforblock's state match is what fails on 40.
fired.playerDropItem: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with SIMACT_PROBE=1 (drivers sdropc40/sdropc51.ps1), through bdsx's hook on ?drop@Player@@. Simbot opens a chest, then its drop virtual is called the way the GameTest dropSelectedItem binding calls it (40 +0x3a0, 51 +0x398, each read off that build's binding). Cancelled: drop returns false and no item entity appears; allowed: true and one appears. This is bdsx's open-container path; the hotbar drop from a client's InventoryTransaction packet is still Q7.
fired.projectileHitBlock: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with BHIT_PROBE=1 (drivers bh40/bh51.ps1). Block::onProjectileHit is inlined into ProjectileComponent::onHit on 1.26, so bdsx raises it from its own onHit hook (projectileHit) with the block at HitResult+0x20: a summoned arrow falling onto a gold block at 44 66 21 printed gold_block 44 66 21 by minecraft:arrow. Not a cancellable event (2024 neither).
fired.lightningHitBlock: 2026-09-24, both builds: tools/block-probe.ts with BHIT_PROBE=1 (drivers bh40/bh51.ps1), through bdsx's hook on ?normalTick@LightningBolt@@ (Block::onLightningHit is inlined there): summon lightning_bolt 48 67 21 onto a lightning rod printed lightning_rod 48 67 21, summon lightning_bolt 46.7 67.2 21.9 printed air 46 67 21 (floored), one event per bolt. Not a cancellable event (2024 neither).
fired.blockDestructionStart: 2026-10-02, both builds: tools/simplayer-probe.ts with SIMQ7_PROBE=1 (drivers simq740/simq751.ps1), through bdsx's hook on ?onStartDestroyBlock@ServerPlayerBlockUseHandler@@ (1.26 inlined sendBlockDestructionStarted into it). Engine-driven: a survival simulated player's simulateDestroyBlock on dirt fires exactly one event at the dirt the next tick (SimulatedPlayer preAiStep's first-tick call) and none on the 16 continue ticks; the dirt breaks 17 ticks after the start. A real client's dig reaches the same function through onBeforeMovementSimulation (not seen yet). work/host-runs/simq740-20261002-111814.txt, simq751-20261002-111814.txt
fired.playerJump: 2026-10-02, both builds: tools/simplayer-probe.ts with SIMQ7_PROBE=1 (drivers simq740/simq751.ps1). Fired by a direct call through the hook -- "simp jumpcall" hands bdsx:JumpExhaustionSystem::_tickEntity (1.26's handleJumpEffects, now the ECS system "JumpExhaustion") simbot's entity id, its ExhaustionComponent and a context holding its EntityRegistry: the event names simbot once per call and the engine body adds 0.05 / 0.2 / 0 exhaustion (plain / sprint bit / creative). What is still missing is an engine-driven jump: simulateJump does not run the system (it never emplaces TriggerJumpRequestComponent), so that needs a real client's jump (Q7). work/host-runs/simq740-20261002-111814.txt, simq751-20261002-111814.txt
fired.blockInteractedWith: 2026-10-02, both builds: tools/livebot-probe.ts scenario useon (drivers lb40/lb51.ps1, LB_RUN=all), through bdsx hook on ?onBlockInteractedWith@VanillaServerGameplayEventListener@@ (slot 8): the harness client right-clicks a chest with an item-use transaction and the event fires once at the chest -3001 67 3002; a crafting table fires none (expected: the engine sends it for chests). work/host-runs/lb40-20261002-153957.txt, lb51-20261002-153957.txt
